conviction_note: The sourced evidence points both ways. Q3 jet fuel ran about $0.9-1.1/gal above the July 2 curve Delta's guide was built on, and Q4 spot is higher again, which argues for a below-consensus Q4/FY guide. Against that, Delta's Trainer refinery earns on record cracks, August ARC fares were +17% and sales +19%, and three peers speaking after Delta last did (AAL, UAL, LUV at Laguna, 16 Sep) described strong Q3 revenue, 'tremendously strong' Q4 bookings and industry capacity cuts. With a balanced skew, moderate short interest and a name that bought a fuel-driven guide withdrawal (+3.75% in April 2026) and sold a beat (-1.81% in July), the sign is close to a coin flip: p_up 48 and abs 6.0 give -0.24. The findings sum to -0.2, so the two measurements agree that there is no edge.
bar: Q3 adjusted EPS consensus about $1.96-2.02, from two-plus agreeing sources: Zacks $1.96 via Parameter (https://parameter.io/delta-air-lines-dal-faces-rising-fuel-costs-as-q3-earnings-approach-october-9/, 2026-10-06; it also cites $1.94 and UBS $1.70), Pluang $2.01 (https://aerohaber.com/delta-air-lines-stock-gains-ahead-of-october-earnings-update/, 2026-09-20) and Benzinga $2.02. The bar sits at or below the LOW end of Delta's own Q3 guide of $2.00-2.50 (mid-teens revenue growth, 11-13% operating margin, all-in fuel ~$3.15/gal off the 2026-07-02 curve with a 5c refinery benefit; https://news.delta.com/sites/default/files/2026-07/delta-air-lines-announces-june-quarter-2026-results.pdf). Revenue consensus is about $17.7bn (Parameter; that is about +16% on adjusted, despite the article's '6%' typo). FY26 consensus is $5.99 (Zacks, per preview) against the company's unchanged $6.50-7.50 guide, which implies Q4 consensus near $1.83 (5.99 - H1 2.20 - Q3 1.96). UBS expects a Q4 guide of $1.25-1.75 at $4.00-4.10 fuel. print_vs_bar_pct is on EPS.
positioning_check: Short interest 26.2M shares at the 2026-09-15 FINRA settlement, up from 25.3M on 08-31; about 4.0% of shares outstanding, 4.9 days to cover, borrow fee 0.4% (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/dal/, read 2026-10-08). The year's high was 29.1M on 06-30. Moderate, not a crowded short. Baseline: 25d skew +0.03 vol points (balanced, priced_direction_lean 'balanced'), put/call open-interest ratio 0.12 (very call-heavy open interest), event-implied move 5.63%, run-up +4.37% over 20d and -2.94% over 5d, 12.8% below the 52-week high. The stock was ~$92-94 in early August (insider sale prices) and $81.66 now, so roughly 12% of fuel de-rating is already in the price.

findings.finding: Q3 jet fuel ran far above the curve Delta guided on. US Gulf Coast kerosene-jet averaged about $3.40 in July, $3.72 in August and $4.39 in September, a Q3 mean of about $3.84/gal. Spot was $2.71 on 2026-07-02, the date of the forward curve behind Delta's ~$3.15 all-in Q3 assumption. On roughly 1.15bn gallons (Q2 was $4.41bn at $3.93/gal, about 1.12bn) that is a gross overrun of roughly $1.0-1.3bn pre-tax, about $1.2-1.5 per share after tax before refinery offsets and fare recapture. Consensus fell only ~11% over 60 days, to ~$1.96 from ~$2.2, and UBS sits at $1.70.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: Delta beat Q2 EPS ($1.56 against ~$1.48) and guided Q3 above consensus, yet closed -1.81% (baseline) as the focus went to fuel-driven YoY EPS decline. Q2 itself beat the TOP of a $1.00-1.50 guide, helped by fuel falling below the $4.30 assumption; this quarter the fuel move runs the other way.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock is ~12% below its early-August level and consensus was cut ~11%. But a $0.25-0.30 consensus cut is small next to a gross ~$1.2-1.5/share fuel overrun, unless analysts assume large refinery and recapture offsets. If the overrun were fully marked, consensus would sit nearer UBS's $1.70 than the $1.96-2.02 the aggregators show.
findings.independence: AAL's CFO said on 2026-09-16 that Q4 fuel runs ~$1/gal above its July projection (https://www.foxbusiness.com/markets/major-airlines-cut-flights-higher-jet-fuel-prices-hit-carriers). The UBS $1.70 estimate is via https://parameter.io/delta-air-lines-dal-faces-rising-fuel-costs-as-q3-earnings-approach-october-9/. This is a proxy: Delta's actual all-in price includes taxes, NY Harbor differentials and the refinery, which is the next finding.

findings.finding: Delta's Trainer refinery (Monroe) is an offset the Q3 guide barely counted. The guide assumed only a 5c/gal refinery benefit. The refinery made $351M of operating income in Q2 2026 even with a mid-June outage (10-Q), and implied Q3 jet cracks against Brent were very wide: ~$59/bbl in July, ~$65 in August, ~$70 in September (FRED jet $3.40/$3.72/$4.39 per gal against Brent $83.8/$91.1/$114.2). A Q3 refinery benefit of 30-45c/gal on ~1.15bn gallons is $350-500M pre-tax, against the ~$60M assumed. UBS cites a 40-45c refinery gain.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history. The refinery helped the Q2 2026 beat above the top of the guide, and the stock still fell 1.81%.
findings.why_not_priced: The preview wire (Zacks via Parameter) still quotes the guide's 'net positive ~5c' refinery framing. Only UBS quantifies 40-45c, and even UBS sits at $1.70. If the refinery offset were widely modelled, the spread between the gross fuel overrun and the consensus cut would be explained in the previews, and it is not.
findings.independence: The Brent series is a different source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=DCOILBRENTEU&cosd=2026-06-01. The UBS refinery view is in the parameter.io preview. Shares the jet series with finding 1, but the two are opposite components of one fuel line and are not double-counted.

findings.finding: The independent revenue series ran at or above Delta's 'mid-teens' Q3 revenue guide. ARC agency air sales were $9.8bn in August 2026, +19% YoY, with average domestic round-trip fare $624 (+17%), premium $1,454 (+11%) and trips +5%. CPI airline fares were +23.4% YoY in August. The offset is that TSA screenings fell 2.7% over the summer and 4.4% in August. Revenue consensus is ~$17.7bn (~+16%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue +14% (top of expectations) with record premium and Amex remuneration of $2.4bn (+16%): the stock fell 1.81%. Revenue strength has not been paid on its own while fuel dominates.
findings.source_date: 2026-09 (August 2026 ARC release; page undated in fetch)
findings.why_not_priced: Industry proxies, not Delta's own numbers. A revenue beat is partly expected given the fare inflation headlines, but consensus at ~+16% sits inside the guide rather than above it. If the market had priced the ARC +19%, revenue consensus would sit above the guided mid-teens.
findings.independence: CPI airline fares +23.4% YoY in August: https://www.travelpulse.com/news/impacting-travel/airfare-prices-surge-as-travel-costs-push-inflation-higher (2026-09-12). Proxy: ARC is agency-settled tickets across all carriers, not Delta.

findings.finding: The Q4/FY guide will be set into fuel well above the July plan. Gulf Coast jet was $4.34/gal on 2026-10-06, versus a $3.84 Q3 mean and $2.71 at the July guide date, and Brent was $125.44 on 2026-10-06 against a $114 September mean, still rising. AAL said Q4 fuel runs ~$1/gal above its July plan. Delta's unchanged FY $6.50-7.50 implies Q4 of $1.80-3.30 against a ~$1.83 consensus. UBS expects a Q4 guide of $1.25-1.75 at $4.00-4.10 fuel, yet current spot plus the usual all-in premium sits at or above that fuel band. A FY cut toward ~$5.25-5.75 against the $5.99 Zacks consensus is the likely shape.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: April 2026: Delta withdrew the FY guide at peak fuel and the stock rose 3.75%. July 2026: it guided Q3 above consensus and reaffirmed FY, and the stock fell 1.81%. In April 2025 the FY guide was withdrawn and the stock rose 23.38%, on the tariff-pause day, so that one is market-driven. On this line the stock has looked through bad guides more than it punished them.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely anticipated. Zacks Rank #5 and falling estimates show the buy side expects a cut, and the stock is ~12% off its August level. What may not be priced is the size: aggregated FY consensus of $5.99 and implied Q4 of ~$1.83 sit above UBS's $1.25-1.75 Q4 band, and fuel spot has not eased since UBS wrote. If the cut were fully priced, consensus would already sit near $5.5.
findings.independence: AAL CFO Devon May, Q4 fuel ~$1/gal above the July projection: https://www.foxbusiness.com/markets/major-airlines-cut-flights-higher-jet-fuel-prices-hit-carriers (2026-09-17). UBS Q4 view: https://parameter.io/delta-air-lines-dal-faces-rising-fuel-costs-as-q3-earnings-approach-october-9/. FY consensus $5.99: Zacks preview via search. Shares the jet series with finding 1, but a different quarter.

findings.finding: Three direct peers spoke at Morgan Stanley Laguna on 2026-09-16, after Delta last guided on 07-10, and all described strong demand. AAL reaffirmed Q3 revenue +16-19% ('Overall for the third quarter, we feel great'). United's CFO called Q4 bookings 'tremendously strong' with 'very little evidence of demand destruction' and is cutting December flights. Southwest kept its Q3 EPS guide because stronger-than-expected fall bookings offset fuel. Industry Q4 capacity cuts support the unit-revenue guide Delta will give.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Delta's July 2026 constructive December-quarter revenue commentary did not stop a -1.81% close. When fuel is the narrative, revenue optimism is partially paid at best.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for three weeks and probably partly behind DAL's +4.4% 20-day run-up. But Delta itself has said nothing since July. If the market had fully carried the peer read to Delta's Q4 RASM, consensus revenue would sit above guide and the Q3 EPS consensus would not have kept falling.
findings.independence: ARC August data (finding 3) is a separate series pointing the same way. Southwest and United statements are in the same Reuters-sourced article, so they count once.

findings.finding: Delta has been silent since 2026-07-10: no 8-K after the Q2 release (EDGAR submissions show only Form 4/144/13G/N-PX since) and no September investor-conference appearance. In September 2025 Delta presented at Morgan Stanley Laguna on 09-11 and reaffirmed its outlook, while in 2026 peers presented and Delta did not.
findings.why_not_priced: It cannot be read either way. Not reaffirming into a $1/gal fuel move may mean Q3 sits below the guide floor, or simply that Delta chose not to speak. Sized at 0 because the absence of a filing is not a cause.

findings.finding: Insiders sold right after the Q2 print. CEO Bastian exercised and sold 206,510 shares at a $92.80 average on 2026-08-04 (~$19.2M), and President Carter, EVP Sear and director Huerta also sold on 08-04/05 at $92.98-94.12. These were option exercises in the open window. The stock is now $81.66.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since August and routine option monetisation. It carries almost no information about this print.
findings.independence: EDGAR submissions show the matching Form 4/144 cluster on 2026-08-03 to 08-06: https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000027904.json

outside_window.finding: United reports Q3 around mid-October (dates listed 10-14 to 10-21). Its read on fuel recapture (it guided 80-90% recapture of the July fuel increase in Q3) is a sector catalyst after Delta's window.
ARC September 2026 ticket sales release, expected around 10-16 based on the 2025 cadence. It is the next independent read on September fares.

baseline_tension: The evidence agrees with the balanced skew. Public fuel negatives on the guide are offset by refinery, fare and peer-demand positives, and the +4.4% 20-day run-up despite rising fuel suggests the market is already looking through the expected guide cut. Nothing here argues against the option market.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (a proxy is filed small): Q3 fuel overrun -1.5 -> -1.0, refinery +0.8 -> +0.5, ARC/CPI revenue +0.6 -> +0.4. All three rest on macro or industry series that Delta has not confirmed for Q3.
Lesson 5 ('no filing' is not a cause): the Delta-silence finding -0.2 -> 0.0, kept as a filed item.
Lessons 1/2 (reaction history on the guidance line): the Q4/FY guide finding -1.5 -> -1.2, because Delta's April 2026 fuel-driven guide withdrawal was bought (+3.75%).

Left standing: the peer-demand finding at +1.2 (a direct counterparty speaking after the company last did, the pattern the file says has paid), the insider finding at -0.1, and p_up 48 / abs 6.0, which already sat near 50 before the file.
